scenarios.title: Keep DHCP replies on the approved server path
scenarios.summary: Protect address offers without blocking the real server, and distinguish an Offer from a recorded lease.
scenarios.objective: Protect the supplied client's VLAN from server replies on user-facing ports while the approved server's full exchange still reaches the client. Observe that an Offer creates no address record, an ACK does, and the record expires after its supplied lease time.
steps: Inspect the supplied network, repair the policy, replay its traffic and check the resulting behavior.
scenarios.explanation: Enable DHCP snooping and inspect VLAN10. Trust the server port, while client and peer remain untrusted. Replay the approved exchange and the unexpected server reply; check that only a delivered ACK records the address and that the supplied expiry sample removes it.
hints: Is the feature enabled for the switch and for the supplied client VLAN? A bypassed exchange is not inspected.
Follow the approved server’s physical path. User-facing ports should not become a way for server replies to enter.
Compare the Offer-only result with the full exchange and expiry sample. Look for an observed record after ACK, not after Offer.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-08: CCNA200-301v1.1/5.7; Catalyst9300 IOS XE Dublin17.12 DHCP chapter2023-07-28. Supplemental Cisco217055 trace2024-06-12 is explicitly16.12.X, not a17.12 runtime test. One supplied access-only LAN; typed initial messages and observed leases, no real packets, allocator, IOS, host interfaces or authentication. Option82 insertion is explicitly disabled in the supplied setup; relay/transformations, other exchange states, rate limits, stacks/trunks and database-agent persistence are excluded. The60-second pending sample cache is a simulator bound, not a protocol timer. Unsupported/ambiguous replies and failed downstream ACK handling diagnose their limits instead of inventing equipment behavior. Checks use separate sample inputs and do not train the displayed state.

example.instructions: In the sample network, enable inspection for the client VLAN and trust the approved server path. Replay the approved exchange, an unexpected server and the Offer-only sample; compare which messages arrive and when an address record appears.

scenarios.title: Compare Ethernet and DHCP client MAC fields
scenarios.summary: Diagnose inconsistent sender details while keeping legitimate DHCP traffic working and understanding the check’s limits.
scenarios.objective: Reject the supplied request whose Ethernet source MAC and DHCP client MAC disagree, while approved exchanges and protection from unexpected servers continue working. Matching sender fields must still be forwarded; this consistency check does not authenticate a device.
steps: Inspect the supplied network, repair the policy, replay its traffic and check the resulting behavior.
scenarios.explanation: Keep snooping active on VLAN10 with only the server path trusted. Enable Compare the two client MAC fields. The mismatched request is rejected, a valid exchange still records its ACK, and matching copied fields are permitted because consistency is not authentication.
hints: Open the mismatched sample and compare Ethernet source MAC with DHCP client MAC before changing settings.
Check the comparison control, while preserving the approved server path and untrusted user ports.
A request with matching copied fields is intentionally permitted by this consistency check. It is not a device-authentication test.
